by.claim: rfc-003-cybersecurity-advisor.md places the proposed role's hours entirely outside engagement work ('None of that is work assigned to a single engagement, and the position sits in the Front Office rather than on a delivery team') and defines no success metric for the role itself, while finance-and-billing.md identifies utilization rate — billable hours over available hours, tracked monthly per chapter and CoE center — as the organization's primary financial-health indicator; because the advisor's coordination, training, and hiring-support work is structurally nonbillable, its output is invisible to the one metric TTS leadership is described as monitoring, leaving the role's value unmeasured in production even after RFC 002's stated aim of getting 'additional engineering... and subject matter expertise into program teams.'
